svg.title: How pq-ucan works
svg.desc: A delegation chain from Alice to Bob to Carol, the byte layout of a token, the supported signature algorithms and signing paths, and the twelve checks the validator runs on an invocation.
svg.text: pq-ucan: how a UCAN chain carries authority
Delegations hand a capability down a chain of did:key principals. An invocation exercises it. The executor validates the whole chain before acting.
1 Delegate, attenuate, invoke
prf names each delegation by CID, root first. The executor looks them up in its own store; a missing one fails with MissingProof.
aud of each hop is the iss of the next
each cmd covers the next, on segment boundaries
sub stays Alice: only the resource owner can be the root
every hop's pol must hold for the invocation args
2 Anatomy of a token

g.text: DAG-CBOR array(2), strict in both directions
by iss, over the bytes of .1, header included
a map with exactly two keys
iss aud sub cmd pol nbf exp nonce meta
an invocation is tagged ucan/inv and adds args, prf

svg.text: CID = CIDv1(dag-cbor, sha2-256(token bytes)), printed as zdpu...
Decoded tokens keep their bytes. Signatures and CIDs are checked over
what was received, never over a re-encoding.
3 Algorithms and signing paths
Any mix of these can sign the hops of one chain. ML-DSA headers stay
provisional until the varsig registry assigns tags.

g.text: wallet or browser key, byte-identical token
header ends a9 02, wire stays DAG-CBOR

svg.text: 4 Validator::validate(invocation)
runs at execution time and stops at the first failure, naming Hop(n) or Invocation
Ok(Proof) the resolved chain, the effective subject and the invocation. Execute from the Proof, never from the bare invocation.
Order: cheap structural checks first for the best diagnostics. Signatures before policy, so no policy runs on a token nobody signed.
Replay last, so a rejected invocation never consumes a nonce. Time bounds allow a clock skew, 60 seconds by default.
